# NEED SME REVIEW
## Inpatient
### ORZID2 GMENU SEPSIS SUSPECTED MENINGITIS
#### SEPSIS WITH SUSPECTED MENINGITIS OR OTHER CNS INFECTION
Consider consulting Infectious Diseases if CNS infection is not strongly
suspected as the main source of infection.
Empirical regimens listed below have broad coverage of likely pathogens based on
infectious site. Resistant gram-negative rods and MRSA coverage is not necessary
in most patients except those with recent isolates of these organisms. Strongly
consider rapid de-escalation of therapy in the first 24-48 hours based on MRSA
nares, isolated pathogen(s), and patient response to therapy. Refer to pathogen
specific sections of the Antimicrobial CDSS for additional treatment
recommendations.
#### Listeria is NOT suspected
Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q12h <AND> vancomycin 15mg/kg IV q12h
#### Listeria IS a concern (Adults >= 50 Years or With Alcoholism, Debilitating Disease, or Impaired Cellular Immunity)
Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q12h <AND> vancomycin 15mg/kg IV q12h <AND> ampicillin 2 gm IV q4h
#### Ceftriaxone or penicillin allergy (see below for severe reactions)
Meropenem 2 gm IV q8h <AND> vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h
#### Severe Beta-lactam reaction
Moxifloxacin 400 mg IV q24h <AND> trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole 5mg/kg (TMP component) IV Q6H <AND> vancomycin 15mg/kg IV q12h
## ER/UC
### ORZID GMENU ER/UC BACT MENING W/O GRM STAIN RES
#### BACTERIAL MENINGITIS (WITHOUT GRAM STAIN RESULTS)
Once a diagnosis of acute bacterial meningitis is considered likely,
antimicrobials should be initiated as soon as possible. Two blood cultures
should be drawn. Lumbar puncture (LP) should be performed in nearly all patients
to obtain cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) for establishing diagnosis and determining
infectious organism/susceptibility. Adjust antimicrobial regimen to optimize
therapy and treatment duration based on pathogen once isolated.
Intravenous dexamethasone therapy improves outcomes for meningitis with
Streptococcus pneumoniae and is recommended for empirical treatment of all
community acquired cases that might be associated with S. pneumoniae.
Dexamethasone must be given before (1 to 20 minutes) with antimicrobials.
If meningococcal meningitis is identified, antimicrobial prophylaxis should be
considered for close contacts. Contact Infectious Diseases/Epidemiology for
advice and assistance.
#### Consult Infectious Diseases
#### Step 1 of Treatment
Dexamethasone 10 mg IV once STAT ($)
(Discontinue if isolated pathogen is not S. pneumoniae)
#### Step 2 of Treatment, Select One of the Following:
#### Treatment for Adults < 50 Years Without Alcoholism, Debilitating Disease, or Any Other Condition Associated with Impaired Cellular Immunity.
Preferred:
Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV once STAT ($) [M] <AND> vancomycin 15mg/kg IV once STAT ($) [R]
Alternative:
[Assessment of beta-lactam reaction](beta-lactam-allergy-assessment)
Meropenem 2 gm IV once STAT ($$) [R] <AND> vancomycin 15 mg/kg once STAT ($) [R]
#### Treatment for Adults >= 50 Years or With Alcoholism, Debilitating Disease, or Impaired Cellular Immunity. Listeria Monocytogenes is One Important Pathogen.
Preferred:
Ampicillin 2 gm IV once STAT ($$) [R] <AND> ceftriaxone 2 gm IV once STAT ($) [M] vancomycin 15mg/kg once STAT ($) [R]
Alternative:
[Assessment of beta-lactam reaction](beta-lactam-allergy-assessment)
Moxifloxacin 400mg IV once STAT ($$) [R,DI] <AND> vancomycin 15mg/kg once STAT ($) [R] <AND> trimethoprim 5 mg/kg - sulfamethoxazole 25 mg/kg IV once STAT ($$$) [R,DI]
ERUC: ORZID GMENU ER/UC BACT MENING W/O GRM STAIN RES
